_comment: OPTIONAL hooks registration to merge into ~/.claude/settings.json (user scope), next to the permissions block from settings.json. Copy the hooks key into your settings.json. Use ABSOLUTE paths: the scripts live in ~/.claude/hooks, not in the project (so ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} does not point at them), and some builds do not expand $HOME/%USERPROFILE% inside hook commands. Replace the ABSOLUTE_HOME placeholder with your real home path (e.g. /home/you or C:/Users/you). guard = recommended security hook; its matcher covers Bash, PowerShell (a separate tool on Windows that Bash rules and a Bash-only matcher miss) and Monitor, plus Write/Edit for the fix-once files and generated agents. format/verify = convenience (allowlist-gated) — delete the blocks you do not want. verify blocks finishing at most CLAUDE_VERIFY_MAX_BLOCKS times in a row (default 3), then shows a still-RED warning. verify is registered twice, same script: Stop runs the checks; UserPromptSubmit only records a turn-start marker - the working-tree state verify last checked, or the current tree on a session's first prompt (no checks, no output, always exit 0) - so a turn in which nothing changed since the last check (e.g. a review in an already-red project) is never blocked, while files written in between (e.g. by a background subagent) are still checked — drop that entry and verify behaves as before (Stop only). WINDOWS: use the .ps1 scripts. Shell-form commands run through Git Bash, or PowerShell when Git Bash is missing (never cmd), so prefer exec form, which spawns powershell.exe directly with no shell and no nested quoting: { "type": "command", "command": "powershell.exe", "args": ["-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-File", "C:/Users/you/.claude/hooks/guard.ps1"] } — same pattern for format.ps1 and verify.ps1 (verify.ps1 in both its UserPromptSubmit and its Stop entry). The shell-form equivalent is: powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "C:\Users\you\.claude\hooks\guard.ps1". The _optional_perPromptDelegationReminder key below is documentation only; if you want it, append its UserPromptSubmit entry to the hooks.UserPromptSubmit array (keep verify's entry there). plan-gate = opt-in convenience (the second Stop entry): while an /implement-plan run still has open plan items or ACs it keeps Claude from finishing, at most CLAUDE_PLAN_GATE_MAX_BLOCKS times in a row (default 3), then shows a 'plan NOT complete' warning. It reads only the plan files named in .claude/plan-gate.local.json, a marker /implement-plan writes with the current session id (a marker from another session is ignored; no marker = exits at once), and runs no project code, so it needs no allowlist. Windows exec form: the same pattern with plan-gate.ps1 and "timeout": 15. Claude Code ends a turn after 8 consecutive Stop-hook continuations, and that cap is shared by all Stop hooks (verify 3 + plan-gate 3 + the opt-in prompt check 1 fits). The _optional_promptCompletionCheck key below is documentation only too: a per-project, opt-in soft check. review-gate (optional, recommended where every change must be reviewed before it lands) denies git commit until a review - code-reviewer + ponytail on the diff, or the inline checklist for a diff of CLAUDE_REVIEW_GATE_INLINE_MAX lines or fewer (default 10) - is recorded for exactly that diff with review-gate.sh --record agents|inline (a binary file always needs the agents); its matcher covers Bash, PowerShell and Monitor, which can all run git commit; it runs only git read commands and keeps its record in a private temp dir, so it needs no allowlist and also suits cloud sessions (the installer's --hooks review-gate); Windows: review-gate.ps1 in exec form like the others.

_optional_perPromptDelegationReminder._comment: OPT-IN, documentation only. The base plugin's per-prompt auto-delegation reminder from before base 1.6.0, verbatim. Base 1.6.0 replaced it with one SessionStart line (startup, clear, compact). To get the per-prompt reminder back as well, add this UserPromptSubmit entry to the hooks.UserPromptSubmit array of ~/.claude/settings.json (next to verify's entry if you use verify). It fires on every prompt and adds its text to context each time, so it costs tokens on every turn. Shell form: the single-quoted echo needs sh or Git Bash. Written for older models: its 'verify findings before finalizing' and 'or a Workflow' wording predate current guidance (over-verification; workflows only when asked) — prefer the base SessionStart line.

hooks.command: echo '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"Standing directive: for substantive tasks, proactively delegate to subagents (Agent tool) or a Workflow and auto-invoke any relevant skill; do not wait to be asked. Scale to task size: answer trivial or conversational prompts inline with no delegation. Prefer parallel subagents for multi-part or multi-file work; verify findings before finalizing."}}'

_optional_promptCompletionCheck._comment: OPT-IN per project, documentation only. A prompt-type Stop hook: at each turn end a small model reads the hook input and asks Claude to continue once when last_assistant_message itself admits requested work left undone (remaining steps, a stub or TODO, guards or tests red or not run). Register it in <project>/.claude/settings.local.json (gitignored; merge the hooks.Stop entry below into that file's hooks.Stop array), not in user scope: it runs no project code, but it costs a small-model call at every turn end (about 0.6-2k input tokens plus up to 80 output) and adds about 1-5 s to each turn end (30 s timeout). It is a soft judge: it sees the hook input, not the files, so verify, plan-gate and the guards stay the hard gates. One nudge per turn at most (stop_hook_active true means ok); plan mode, questions to the owner and turns with background tasks are exempt. It counts toward the 8-continuation cap shared by all Stop hooks (verify 3 + plan-gate 3 + this 1).

hooks.prompt:
You decide whether Claude may end its turn. Hook input JSON: $ARGUMENTS

Return {"ok": true} if any of these holds: stop_hook_active is true; permission_mode is "plan"; background_tasks is non-empty; last_assistant_message asks the user a question, asks for approval or a decision, or reports a blocker only the user can resolve; the turn answered a question and delivered no work.
Otherwise return {"ok": false, "reason": "<the specific unfinished items, at most 3 short bullets>"} only when last_assistant_message itself shows requested work left undone that Claude could do now: it lists remaining or next steps it did not do, says it skipped, stubbed, or left a TODO or placeholder, or reports guards or tests red or not run after edits.
When unsure, return {"ok": true}. Do not ask for polish, refactors, extra tests or scope beyond the request. Reply with JSON only.
